The appellant was a tenant of a part of a building in the State of Madras. The lease was granted by the State Government to the appellant on January 10, 1942, and the lease was granted to him on September 7, 1949. The lease continued to be in force till February 1, 1947, and the appellant applied to the Collector for confirmation of the lease. The Collector granted the lease to the appellant. The appellant applied to be satisfied that the lease was not valid. The Collector refused to grant the lease. On appeal the Collector held that the lease had been terminated by the appellant and the appellant was entitled to the grant of the lease and the appellant had no right to terminate the lease. In appeal to this Court, it was contended on behalf of the appellant that the lease did not amount to a lease of the land and that the lease could not be terminated without any compensation under the second proviso to section 20(1) of the Abolition Act. Held, that the lease in the present case was not a lease of land but was a lease of a land and the lease in favour of the appellant was not a grant of a lease of any land. The lease in the instant case was not an lease of land and the appellant could not be said to have been entitled to the lease. Held, further, that the appellant was a lessee of a part and parcel of a building and was entitled to a lease for a period of 20 years commencing from February 1,1945, and the lessee was entitled to be paid the lease amount to the lease and that the lessee was not entitled to the renewal of the lease, and the grant of lease was not a condition of the lease but a lease of an additional lease of land. The grant of lease in favour was not a mere lease of land, and the lessor was not entitled under the terms of the lease to terminate the tenancy. The lease did not attract the operation of the second proviso. The lease had to be renewed at the option of the lessee for one year. The lease could not, in our view, be terminated without compensation under the third proviso. The second proviso to the lease was invalid as it was made unconditional by the lessee. The second condition was that the lessee would be entitled to the lessee 's lease for a further period not exceeding the duration of the original lease. The second clause in the lease was void as against the Government without any further necessity for any overt act to be done by the Government to avoid the same.
